targets.notes: Result-export path. On a 20,000-value Decimal column the body is a Python list comprehension around Decimal.quantize, and DataFrame.dropna pays an object-dtype NA scan (pandas _isna_string_dtype) even when nothing is missing. cProfile puts about half the time in that Python/pandas wrapper rather than in the rounding rule. Cent rounding must stay ROUND_HALF_UP.

targets.native_test_cmd: python -m pytest tests/test_scope.py -k "symbol_array_store_from_frame or symbol_array_store_pickle" -p no:randomly
targets.notes: Flat OHLCV ingress used by every backtest store build. On 50 symbols x 1,260 days, cProfile shows about 70% of the time in np.unique(return_inverse=True) argsorting the repeated symbol strings (50 labels, 63k rows). A hash factorize, or run-length grouping when the frame is already symbol-major, avoids that string sort. Float columns are also materialized twice: to_numpy(copy=True) into an array that is then discarded, then copied again into the column stack.

Walkforward history/train/test slicing. Each call re-checks that the target window and every symbol's dates are sorted (np.all over the full date array) and then copies every column with np.array(..., copy=True), including the contiguous-range branch. The store builder already sorts dates, and a history window is a contiguous span, so those scans and per-column copies repeat. The bench times five slices of one 120-symbol x 2,000-date window because a single slice is only ~2.5ms and its run-to-run spread exceeds 3%.
